notes: The current OICR pages are reachable and give a useful side-by-side price comparison. archive.ph is blocked for this fetch tool ('unable to fetch from archive.ph'), so I could not open any 2024 or 2025 snapshots. The live Illumina and Ultima prices carry no dates tied to the Ultima listing. That means I cannot say whether Illumina prices fell after Ultima was added. Illumina WGS rows are 'valid as of May 2024' and the NovaSeq X sequencing-only lane is 'valid as of May 2025'. The Ultima table has no date. I used 3 fetches plus 1 search, and the pages opened were genomics.oicr.on.ca/, /services/ and /ultima-sequencing/. This is a single dated snapshot, not a history. I did not use the Wayback Machine, as instructed.
how_to_mine: Retrieve archive.ph snapshots of genomics.oicr.on.ca/services/ and /ultima-sequencing/ (2024, 2025, 2026) in a browser or a tool that can reach archive.ph. Record the 'valid as of' dates and the Illumina 30X/80X WGS, X 10B lane and Ultima wafer / 30X WGS prices for each snapshot. A diff of the Illumina rows between snapshots would show whether they were cut after the Ultima listing appeared. Also try Google cache or Common Crawl (index.commoncrawl.org) for dated copies of the same URLs. Last resort: ask OICR via /contact-us/ for historical price sheets.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: A Canadian academic genomics core lists Ultima 30X WGS at roughly a third of its Illumina price, which pressures Illumina research pricing.
items.detail: OICR Genomics (CAD, current page, © 2026) lists Illumina 30X WGS at $1,181 (fastq only) and $1,241 (standard pipeline), against Ultima 30X WGS at $435 (min 20 samples) and 80X WGS at $920 vs Illumina $2,613. That is Ultima at about 37% of the Illumina price at 30X (about 35% at 80X). These are service prices that include library prep and overhead, and Ultima is academic-only with minimum orders. The Illumina rows are dated May 2024 and the Ultima rows are undated, so the gap is a snapshot, not a trend.
items.date: 2026 (page footer); Illumina rows valid as of May 2024
items.quote: first Canadian Certified Ultima Service Provider
items.why_new: This is a core-facility side-by-side of full WGS service prices (Ultima vs Illumina) that the known list does not include; the known core lists cover only Illumina lane $/Gb.

items.label: 2B
items.claim: A core lane price shows Illumina X 10B at CAD $2,734 against an Ultima 10B wafer at CAD $5,130 (two-wafer minimum), so Ultima is not cheaper at raw run level.
items.detail: OICR lists a NovaSeq X 10B (300 cycle) lane at $2,734 (sequencing-only table valid as of May 2025) and an Ultima 10B wafer at $5,130 with a 2-wafer minimum. Roughly, at similar nominal 10B output the Illumina lane is the cheaper raw run. Ultima's advantage appears only in the per-genome service price ($435 vs $1,181 for 30X), so it is likely driven by throughput per run and library/prep economics. This cuts against a simple 'Ultima is cheaper per run' reading. It is a mixed signal for 2B. I tag it supports only because it shows the core is repricing the genome service, not lanes.
items.why_new: This gives a Canadian core X 10B lane price and an Ultima wafer price on the same page; neither was in the known core-price lists.
